workload.note: wide prefix with two different final questions

analysis.conclusion: Native GPU prefix cache is fastest for hot prefixes; external connector beats recompute but adds first-store and disk-load overhead. Use native for hot, connector for cold/persistent/tenant-isolated cache.

optimizationDirections: Hybrid routing: native prefix cache for hot prefixes, external connector for cold/persisted/large prefixes.
Reduce connector load overhead: pinned host buffers, async/overlapped KV load, faster NVMe, uncompressed hot path.
Measure prefix-length crossover: externalize only above a threshold where disk load beats recompute.
Lower vLLM gpu_memory_utilization and rely on external cache to free GPU for other models.
Keep gzip for cold storage only; gzip increases hit latency significantly.
Batch/group external KV loads for multi-prefix requests; avoid per-layer sequential file IO.
caveats: Single process; API latency includes network stack overhead.
1856-token prefix workload; crossover thresholds not yet measured.
Connector is a prototype with disk safetensors.
